Graham Whitfield’s gym club locker in the tower and his office (with the branch chief’s approval):

· In the squash bag, the special programmes’ manual trigger key for the fire suppression system; Graham Whitfield’s fingerprint on the key.

· Chair: Anne-Marie Leduc (in the boardroom).

The victim’s assistant.

He was in the archive all day, going through old policy files. ‘They all pay the same beneficiary, Mirela; the name sounds like an institution, but it isn’t one, it’s a woman,’ he said. He was going to present it at the meeting. On his way out in the evening he said, ‘Whitfield’s here tonight; he says he’s in Toronto, but I saw his car downstairs.’ He smiled, and I laughed.

On the night of 25 November 2030, on the 42nd floor of Tour Laurentide in Montreal, Laurentide Réassurance’s chief actuary Daniel Kovač (54) was found dead in the data archive room. The room’s fire suppression gas had been released; the door was locked from outside.

The night security supervisor Luc-Antoine Renaud found the body at 22.05, responding to the alarm. On the floor that evening: the board meeting chaired by the managing director Anne-Marie Leduc (most members by video link), the vice-president for special programmes Graham Whitfield, and the data centre technician Chidi Obi. The victim’s assistant Mirela Popescu had left at 19.00.

The day before, the victim had written to the bube Montreal — Mile End branch.
INCIDENT REPORT
Request the autopsy report
Request permission to search the vice-president’s gym locker and office
Request the board meeting minutes

The minutes were a decoy: seven witnesses saw the screen, but not the ten minutes of darkness. Security, the technician and the assistant filled the gap with the floor, the key and the car. The search found the key in the squash bag and the payment instructions in the office.
Seven people saw him on screen. None of them asked about the camera that was off.
Tour Laurentide — November 2030

For fourteen years Laurentide Réassurance’s ‘special programmes’ division reinsured fake or inflated policies, from the Mile End bakery to the silo, and diverted the claim payouts to the ‘bube International Liaison Programme’ — that is, to Edda Varga. The chief actuary Daniel Kovač was going to present this to the board. The vice-president Graham Whitfield turned his camera off for ten minutes during the meeting he joined ‘from Toronto’, locked Kovač in the archive and released the gas by hand.
Who killed Daniel Kovač?

Anne-Marie Leduc
Chidi Obi
Graham Whitfield
Vice-president for special programmes.
Special programmes is the company’s most profitable division.
No.
Look at the minutes: connected from eight to half past nine. Seven witnesses. A man can’t be in two places at once.

I wasn’t in Toronto; I was in the small meeting room on the forty-second floor. I turned the camera off for ten minutes. If Daniel presented his table, it would come out what the ‘Liaison Programme’ was, and whose it was. I met Edda fifteen years ago in London; ‘You write the policy, we’ll do the rest,’ she said. And it was always like that: in Mile End, at the silo, in the snowstorm, always. I wrote to her one last time: ‘Montreal is closed.’ The reply came from Melbourne, for the first time: ‘I know.’
You locked Daniel in the archive.
I was in the meeting, an hour and a half, seven people saw me on screen. Daniel worked too hard; alone in the archive, at night, a system fault. Tragic.
He straightens the knot of his tie with two fingers.
